html:
The Srebrenica massacre was the killing of more than 8,000 Bosniak men and boys by Bosnian Serb forces under Ratko Mladić in July 1995, after they took the town of Srebrenica in eastern Bosnia.

Srebrenica had been declared a United Nations safe area, guarded by a small Dutch battalion that did not resist. Women and children were bussed away while men were taken to fields, schools and warehouses and shot, and the bodies were later moved to hide them. International courts have ruled the massacre a genocide, and Mladić and the Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadžić were sentenced to life in prison. The massacre led to NATO bombing and the end of the Bosnian War at Dayton. 11 July is remembered across Bosnia.
sum: The Srebrenica massacre was the killing of more than 8,000 Bosniak men and boys by Bosnian Serb forces under Ratko Mladić in July 1995, after they took the town of Srebrenica in eastern Bosnia.
